open_prs.body:
**Draft. Yours to merge (R-SEMH01: no-ff, never squash).** Micro-PR — QA only.

Retains the Pass TW-1 checks and measured browser evidence in-repo so they outlive the session that produced them. **No runtime file is touched.**

| | |
|---|---|
| Base | `298c4381982ef44e69f6b4f20b9dc015bb5ed96d` (main, post PR #3) |
| Tip | `b5173398e35a1b8b5ea35ef3c03f5782759a2795` |
| Diff | **32 files added, 0 modified, 0 deleted** |
| Scope | `qa/teacher-upgrade/**` + `.github/workflows/teacher-upgrade-contract.yml` — **0 files outside those two paths** |

## The one thing worth reading

**`proposed/` mirrors merged `main`, not the pack as shipped.** This is load-bearing, not an oversight.

`apply_teacher_upgrade.py` treats `proposed/` as the source of truth for the five upgrade-owned files. Had the pack's originals been retained, **re-running the installer against this repo would have tried to revert C1, C5 and C6** — silently undoing the hud loader, the UAS wording and the per-device copy.

As retained, a re-run reports **zero changed files**:

```
python qa/teacher-upgrade/tools/apply_teacher_upgrade.py .
→ changedFileCount: 0
```

`--strict-baseline` now refuses, correctly — the source blobs have legitimately moved past the audited baseline. That refusal is the tool working.

## The two disclosed harness fixes, now durable

Both in `tests/browser_smoke.py`. Neither weakens a gate.

1. **The C5 fixture asserted the behaviour the estate ruling forbids.** It selected `aqa-uas` and typed the scheme's own name, `"Unit Award Scheme"`, into the **Level / size** box — the exact confusion the ruling corrects. The assertion was not deleted; it was replaced with a **stricter positive control** (`UAS has no level (C5)`) that fails if the Level field is ever editable or non-empty while UAS is active. The harness therefore reports **19 checks, not 18**.
2. **The fixture site served no `/hud.js`.** C1 gave Data Manager the loader all 28 other studios carry; `/hud.js` is served from the domain root, not this repo, so the isolated fixture 404ed and the "no console errors" assertion failed against an environment that doesn't exist in production. A stub is written into the fixture site; the assertion is untouched.

## Workflow is manual-only

`workflow_dispatch` **only** — verified by parsing the YAML, not grepping: `{'workflow_dispatch': None}`. The shipped template also carried a `pull_request:` trigger; **I removed it**. It never runs on push or PR. Start it from the Actions tab.

## Gates on the final tree

- Installer idempotent vs `main`: **0 changed files**
- `test_apply_teacher_upgrade.py` / `test_verify_teacher_upgrade.py`: **PASS / PASS** from the retained location
- `verify_teacher_upgrade.py .`: **44 passed, 0 warnings, 0 failures**
- `sha256sum -c MANIFEST.sha256`: **all 30 entries OK**
- Workflow triggers: `['workflow_dispatch']`
- `__pycache__`/`.pyc` excluded (a `.gitignore` prevents recurrence)

## Two honest caveats

**`MANIFEST.sha256` was regenerated** over the retained tree, because `proposed/`, `tests/` and `reports/` have all legitimately changed. It passes here, but it **no longer attests to the original published archive** — that check ran and passed during Pass TW-1 against `8ee7c95f…711a9`. Recorded in `RETENTION_NOTE.md`.

**`reports/` holds my measured evidence, not the pack's claims** — 19/19 against the corrected files. The pack's 18/18 was independently reproduced before corrections, not copied.

## Still outstanding (unchanged)

- **Tools-hub card** for Data Manager belongs in the main site repo (`tools/index.html`, utilities 11→12). Cross-repo, not done.
- Estate **theme port** stays parked; C2 is a seed-read only.

**Do not merge — Matt merges.** Job 5 of the card-art brief. Pairs with [mattroper1977.github.io#13](https://github.com/MattRoper1977/mattroper1977.github.io/pull/13). ## The disagreement The lead paragraph said **"Twenty-eight single-file studios"**. The pill a few lines below said **"30 of 30 studios"**. **The pill was right.** It counts `apps.json`, which holds 30 studios across seven spaces with no duplicates: ``` Teacher tools 9 · Make & create 6 · Art & design 5 · Documents 1 Learn & organise 6 · Calm corner 2 · Play & explore 1 = 30 ``` The prose was hand-written and had drifted. ## Why not just write 30 Because that is what was done at 28, and again at 29, and it broke both times. The brief was explicit that the fix has to be structural. So the number is now **generated from the same `apps.json` the pill counts** and written into a span in the sentence. The sentence stays handwritten for its rhythm; only the number in it is derived: ```html

Your offline creative workshop. Thirty single-file studios that run straight from the browser — …

``` `inWords()` keeps it a word rather than a digit, so the line still reads "Thirty single-file studios". Above 99 it falls back to the digit, which reads worse but is never wrong. ## Verified by making it move Added a studio to `apps.json`, reloaded, and watched both numbers track together: ``` before lead "Thirty" pill "30 of 30 studios" after lead "Thirty-one" pill "31 of 31 studios" ``` Restored afterwards — `apps.json` is unchanged in this PR. ## The other three copies Three more stale counts lived in `mattroper1977.github.io`: `site.json` said 28, `tools/index.html` said 29, `next/apps.html` said 29. That repo has no access to `apps.json` at build time, so any number there is a hand-copy that drifts the moment a studio is added. It now states none — "every studio in the collection", "the creator studios". Handled in that repo's PR. A number nobody owns is worse than no number. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_017G7d7W8Q4AhMAM1wGY8Pfh --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_017G7d7W8Q4AhMAM1wGY8Pfh)_ --- ## Census disposition — 2026-08-17 · EXEMPT WHILE HELD Appended by the close-everything pass. Nothing above this line was altered. **This PR runs zero check runs, and that is correct rather than a defect.** It is held by its own first line — *"Do not merge — Matt merges"* — so nothing is asking to merge, and a PR with no merge request accurately has no CI result. **Cause, derived rather than guessed:** **CONFLICTED**. `mergeable_state` is `dirty`, so GitHub can build no merge ref — and with no merge ref nothing fires, however the filters are written. **No change to any workflow could give this PR a check while it is in that state.** Underneath the conflict there is a second, independent reason, recorded so it is not discovered again later: this repo has four workflows, and none of them would match this diff anyway. `mbm-cross-estate-unification.yml` (9 `paths:` entries) and `theme-parity.yml` (3) match nothing in a one-file change to the Creator Hub lead paragraph; `stealth-live-verify.yml` and `wave-ohm-origin-drive.yml` are `workflow_dispatch`-only. Two stacked causes, in the order they would have to be fixed. **Consequence:** merging current `main` in resolves the conflict, but that alone still yields zero checks here — the path filters would have to gain an entry for this file, or a catch-all workflow would have to exist in this repo as one now does in Lessons. **Not rebased, not merged, not closed.** Recorded so the next census does not re-raise it as an undeclared finding. It remains declared in `tools/zero_check_baseline.json` in the Lessons repo.

open_prs.body:
## C0's scope fence is the position now, not a holding pattern

**Ruled.** The deciding question was never whether the content is too violent. By the standard of what fifteen-year-olds already play it plainly is not, and the enemies are an insectoid Brood and a construct boss rather than people — a genuine mitigator, not pretended away.

The question is: **should a teacher publish, under his own name, on the site his SEMH pupils reach through lesson links, a game set in a school under attack with a mode called PROTOCOL LOCKDOWN?** Lockdown is not a neutral word in a school building. It names a drill those pupils have stood through, and for some of them it will name more than a drill. Parking costs nothing; unpublishing is much harder than not publishing.

**No route. No manifest entry. No card, hue, genre, feel tag, take, `TOP` or `hero`. No link from anywhere.** The `C0` gate asserts that against the canonical shelf record, both audience pages and the curation renderer, and reports **INCONCLUSIVE, never a pass**, if it cannot read one of them. Its purpose is to go red if anyone ever adds the route.

**If it is ever wanted on the shelf, the route is a re-skin, not a debate about content.** Strip the school framing — PROTOCOL LOCKDOWN, the Academy, the Dean's Exam, the Arch-Provost, the Academic Transcript — and it becomes an ordinary tactical combat game that publishes on ordinary merits. That is a content commission with its own budget.

**The technical work proceeds regardless.** A parked artefact with a known boot-kill is still a liability, and these fixes are the reference material for the next pack that repeats them.

## Provenance

The prototype at v0.1.0 has **0 `localStorage` calls, 0 normalizers and 0 `__COA_QA`**. Every defect fixed below was introduced by the PRO release's own *"Reliability and hardening"* work.

## C1 — the null-parse boot kill

`safeParse` returns `JSON.parse('null')` → `null`, which is **not `undefined`**, so the `raw={}` default parameter never fired and the first property read threw. Scope measured, not assumed: `settings=BREAKS · profile=BREAKS · activeRun=fine`.

The guard goes **inside both normalizers** so every future caller inherits it, and it guards on **shape**, not on `undefined` — the whole lesson of the defect.

**Why the release report claimed a pass:** its own `qa/TEST_SUMMARY.json` records the injected settings as a well-formed **object** with bad **values**. The top-level **type** was never varied. This varies it: 7 shapes × 3 keys = **21 cases**; release fails 2.

## C2 — unvalidated URL parameters

Repair (1): the autostart block existed only to serve the QA harness C3 removes, so it went with it. **All five bad parameter sets break release; none breaks this build.**

## C3 — the ungated QA hook

`window.__COA_QA` shipped live with `grant`, `setPlayer`, `hurt`, `teleport`, `spawn`, `strike`, `setStats` — rewriting the run **and the persistent Academic Transcript**. Removed in full.

**The cost was paid rather than dodged:** every gate here drives the game through the DOM and real events. `C3c` walks mode → chassis → overclock → Deploy and asserts the canvas is *painting*, for each of the three modes and each of the four chassis — 4 configurations covering the **union**, stated as such rather than implied to be the 12-case cross product.

## C4 — subtitle / HUD collision

The clearance is **derived from the same expression the draw path uses**, and the predicate asserts a real **8 px margin** rather than the absence of intersection. Under that: release fails **8 of 8** viewport/largeHud combinations, this build **0 of 8**, with 12 px everywhere.

That correction mattered — `overlap === 0` was passing on the two wide combinations where a fixed value abutted the HUD at exactly zero gap. *Touching is not clearing.*

## The Academic Transcript — ruled

**No persistent graded record attached to a pupil's name.** The estate already settled this in its own governance copy — *"not grades, diagnoses"* — and holding that line in the science instruments while dropping it the moment the same pupils meet a game would be incoherent. For an SEMH cohort a stored DISTINCTION/MERIT/PASS is a shame trigger they cannot escape by playing better.

**Record what was done and observed, not what it was worth.** Not implemented here — the game is parked, so the ruling is recorded against it and lands with the re-skin if that is commissioned.

## Deliberately not done

Storage keys **not renamed** (`COA-TRANSCRIPT-1` may be in the wild; atomic migration unproven). `canonical` omitted while C0 stands. Splash, way home, title and `og:` need shelf conventions. **Mode names and in-game copy untouched.**

## Discipline

Ten transforms, **all watched**, measured:

```
Y1a  watched      C1->CONTROL
Y1b  watched      C1->CONTROL
Y2   watched      C2->CONTROL C3b->CONTROL
Y3   watched      C3a->CONTROL
Y4a  watched      C4->CONTROL
Y4b  watched      C4->CONTROL
Y4c  watched      C4->CONTROL
Y4d  LOAD-BEARING C3c->REGRESSION C4->CONTROL
Y5d  watched      C5.4->CONTROL
Y5e1 watched      C5.5a->CONTROL
```

`Y4d` is LOAD-BEARING per R0.11: `Y4c` calls the helper it defines, so its sole removal crashes the build and the red measures the crash rather than the behaviour.

### Correction to an earlier version of this description

An earlier version asserted that `Y4d` "is labelled LOAD-BEARING per R0.11". **It was not, and the tool could not have labelled it.** The check grepped the verdicts file for `ERR->ERROR`, but that file stores `ERR ERROR` — the arrow exists only in the diff string built separately for display. So the label could never fire, on this tool or the Chemistry Lab's, and every load-bearing transform printed as an ordinary `watched`.

That is a gate that silently never ran, in the very code added to record R0.11 — the tenth such this pass, and the first introduced *while writing the rule about them*. Fixed to test the diff string, and the table above is the measured output rather than the asserted one.

The same commit adds a lock on the evidence file, because two matrix runs wrote into one concurrently and left an interleaved artefact with a half-line in it.
open_prs.title: [PARKED — DO NOT MERGE, RULED] Class of Ashes: fix what the hardening pass broke

open_prs.body:
## Do not merge. This is the reference diff for v0.4.1.

v0.4 forks the **unpatched** v0.3 baseline with all six defects surviving verbatim. Merging this would put a fixed 5-bench file and an unfixed 13-bench file in the estate at once, with the unfixed one superseding. So this branch exists to be *re-applied*, not landed.

**Route is ruled and is not what holds it:** the **Lessons repo, as a science practical instrument, co-located with the FieldOps labs**. Not the Games shelf, not Apps/Teacher tools. The precedent was already set — FieldOps split labs 01–04 into Lessons beside the science and sent only the Teacher Studio to Apps, because a lab is a lesson instrument and a studio is a teacher tool. **VCL is a lab**: pupils do the practical, it carries a 40-minute Introduce→Explore→Do arc, it is not teacher-directed.

Two things sequence the landing: the FieldOps placement has not merged, so the co-location path does not exist yet; and the route attaches to v0.4.1.

---

## V1 — the bench rewarded the procedure it teaches against

`microResolve` rebuilt each well from an **order-independent ion pool** on every drop, and the sequencing check was presence-only. Silver nitrate first, then nitric acid, gave a **byte-identical clean positive** to doing it correctly, with **no warning at all** — while the left panel of that same bench teaches the correct order and its own question 3 asks why it matters.

**The reaction model is untouched. Only the predicate changed** — `w.drops` was already an ordered array. All four reversed orders now warn; all four correct orders keep their clean positive.

## V2 — the URL carries the setup. It never carries the pupil's work.

**Ruled, and it overturns my earlier call.** I kept the evidence note in the hash because with no `localStorage` anywhere the URL is this app's only persistence. True, and not the deciding fact: **Share hands the URL out**, so a teacher sharing a bench setup would be shipping whichever pupil's note and answers were last typed.

Out of `serialisableState()`: the **name**, the **note**, the **written answers**. *(v0.4's drawing strokes belong in that list when this is re-applied.)* Retained: bench, apparatus, sample codes, teacher fault injection.

The cost is real and the captions carry it rather than hide it — the note's label now says it is not saved and not shared, and tells a pupil to Print or Export before closing the tab. The name's caption was never rewritten; the code was made to match what it already promised.

That makes **Print and Export JSON the only place the work survives**, which `V2b` and `V2g` assert for all three. That control has caught the same defect **twice**: once when the first cut emptied the name out of the export, and again when the widened ruling took the answers with it — the second catch only happened because the first left an assertion behind.

## V3 — the state URL

| | release | staging |
|---|---|---|
| fresh load | 3,814 | **26** |
| each bench, untouched | 3,834–3,841 | 81–107 |
| realistic 40-minute session | 8,094 | **769** |

Most of that last figure is the **ruling**, not the encoding: the answers were the bulkiest growing payload, so a large part of V3 arrives free with the privacy decision.

The roundtrip control is split in two — *"the link still works"* and *"the link stopped carrying pupil writing"* are different claims, and checking only the first would have missed the ruling entirely. `V3-legacy` also asserts a link minted by the **release** build still opens here.

## V4 · V5 · V6

- `.drop-pill` had **no CSS rule at all**. Gap at 390 px and 1440 px: **0 px → 6 px**.
- Marking was negation-blind — release marks **6 of 8** negated near-misses correct. Now zero. Keyword items compare against a model answer and the button reads **Compare**; the four items checking a **computed value** keep their verdict. Covers **eight** items, not six.
- Reduced motion seeded from the OS. **17** unnamed controls across five benches → **0**, under a stated predicate (the "3" in the handover note is the default bench under a looser one).
- **Viewport was already correct. Untouched, and asserted untouched.**

## The printed practical record — ruled

**No persistent graded record attached to a pupil's name.** VCL's named artefact is the printed practical record, so it keeps observations, procedure and the evidence note, and carries **no verdict**. `V2h` searches the whole print sheet for a grade word or a tick and finds none on **both** trees — it was already true, and is watched now, which is the difference between a property and a guarantee. The verdict this app *did* pronounce was in the marking, and V5 removed it.

## Discipline — measured

Eighteen named exact-string transforms; drop all eighteen → `release/` byte for byte; **drop each one → a verdict changes**:

```
X1a  watched        X2d  watched        X5a  LOAD-BEARING
X1b  watched        X3a  watched        X5b  watched
X1c  LOAD-BEARING   X3c  watched        X6c  watched
X2a  watched        X3d  watched        X6d1 watched
X2b  watched        X3e  watched        X6d2 watched
X2c  watched        X4   watched        X6d3 watched
```

`X1c` and `X5a` are **LOAD-BEARING** per R0.11: `X1a`/`X1b` call the `acidFirst` predicate one defines and `X5b`'s template references the table the other defines, so their sole removal crashes the build and the red measures the crash rather than the behaviour. **That label had never applied before this run** — it grepped the verdicts file for `ERR->ERROR`, which stores `ERR ERROR`; the arrow exists only in the separately-built diff string. See #120.

`X2a`'s row is worth reading: dropping it reddens `V2a`, `V2c`, `V2g` and `V3-roundtrip-work` together, because the privacy ruling widened what that one transform removes and each part has its own assertion.

A nineteenth transform was written and deleted after the matrix reported it unwatched and it turned out to protect nothing.

Everything is driven through the page's own DOM and real events.

## What merges (not this PR's held content)

### 1 · `_semh2/proposed_dt_dust_ht.diff` — OPEN_ITEMS #18 re-emitted at HEAD (§4)
4 files, 7 hunks; wording from the ruled accounts in `quality/toolkits/SAFETY_CONTENT_GATE.md`. **No drift** — every TK-1-located target string present exactly once at HEAD. PENDING-LOCAL-APPROVAL intact; the D&T lead + H&S/COSHH ledger rows govern. `BUILD_DT_W5`: the blanket dust-mask line becomes prevent → extract → RPE with the named stop condition; "the door stays open" becomes the centre's-arrangements form. `W1/W2/W3` cut-list: HT-as-the-wood-decision becomes the six-check acceptance (reject on any one failure, even HT-stamped). `W2/W3` pre-tool line: "accepted wood only". printPack id lists and Lundy-page text untouched (OPEN_ITEMS #7 / R-A07 BOUNDARY).

### 2 · `_semh2/proposed_tbc_unit_code_hide.diff` — the derived 25 (§5.1)
Derivation: tracked `unit code: TBC` = 30 files − 5 documentation/tooling carriers = **25 Science_Teesside lesson files** (Build 5 · Grow 5 · Launch 15), exactly one instance each, all on the witness-statement print header. The hide is a **marked, byte-reversible HTML comment** (`semh2-hide (reversible; restore on Cheryl's confirmation): …`) — no layout break, greppable, restores by deleting the comment markers. Pupil-adjacent print surfaces → Matt's read stands.

### 3 · `_semh2/proposed_constructed_source_labels.diff` — LAUNCH Humanities (§5.2)
Derived over the seven non-assessed LAUNCH_HUM decks (assessed W7 untouched): **W1** — the seven-document teaching archive (port tonnage ledger 1901–09 · 1907 quay photograph · 'Bustling dock' postcard · 1908 strike report · 1905 trade directory · docker's 1950 memoir · 1906 crane minutes); **W3** — the NOP specimen attributions ('Written at the works office, 1871' and siblings); **W4** — the paired 1915/2015 photographs (framing device, lightest instance). **W2/W5/W8: none. W6's "90,000 by 1901" judged REAL** (the census figure is a fact citation — enumerated so the judgement is visible, not silently skipped). One wording style — *"reconstructed from period records for this lesson"* — one label per presenting surface (screen + print twin), teaching not undermined: the labels state the substance reflects Teesside's documented history.

## Gates at branch tip `0c0f048`

Diff confinement: the §3 file + 3 ledgers + `_semh2/` docs, nothing else · sentinels **50 / 98** (tracked `*.html` containing the literal marker), unmoved · assessed `*_HUM_W7` pair and the 6 D&T decks byte-identical to base · `node --check` + jsdom clean on the edited file · zero storage/egress added · ledgers append-only, rows extended in place with originals preserved, no renumbering · zero Progress marks by SVG content.

Closes `_close/OPEN_ITEMS.md` **#19**. Base `8f4f9b1`. One file, +48/−1. Rollback: `git revert -m 1` on the merge commit, or `8f4f9b1`.

The other seven `Art_Teesside` evidence packs gained the large-print option in **#41** (`tk1-access`, merged). That branch has since merged, so the file is free and the eighth pack gets the same recipe.

Every pt size **×1.5 with an 11.5pt floor**, the fixed page height released so sheets paginate rather than clip, dense grids single-columned. **Content is identical in both renders** — only type and spacing change.

The base size was deliberately **not** simply raised: forcing 11.5pt into a fixed one-page-per-week A4 layout produces a pack with content **missing**, and the loss would be silent.

The **29 rules are derived from this file's own CSS**, not hand-listed — #41's method, and the reason a selector cannot be missed or silently go stale. This file's ladder is the same one the audit found, floor **6.6pt**, worse than the reported "approximately 7–9pt".

**One derivation artefact caught:** the bare `body` selector would have produced `body.lp body`, which matches nothing. It becomes `body.lp`. Asserted at **0** occurrences of the broken form.

|---|---|

No browser in this container. Print geometry cannot be measured here, and **a skipped gate is unverified, never passed**. That is what the hold above is for.

## Flagged, not silently fixed

This pack does **not** carry the alternative-evidence wording the other seven gained in #41 — the *"any evidence form counts"* line and *"**no part of this award requires handwriting**"*. Verified absent here.

So the eighth pack's adviser currently sees a **weaker accessibility statement than the other seven**. That is adviser-facing wording, outside this branch's scope, and it is reported for you rather than added on my judgement. Say the word and it's a one-line follow-up.

open_prs.body:
The staleness sweep proved this instrument **could not detect drift at all** — a scratch copy given genuinely stale content passed it, exit 0. Its greens carried no information, which is worse than having no check. The estate's own word for that is a **false zero**, and this one was live and invokable.

## The defect

`repair()` only ever looks for the string it wants to replace:

```python
for before, after in PATCHES:
    if after in html: continue
    html = html.replace(before, after)
```

A lesson carrying a **third** state — an older revision of a block this file owns — matches neither `before` nor `after`. `repair()` changes nothing, and `--check` prints `ok`.

## The fix

Freshness is now asserted separately and **on content**. `GENERATED_REGIONS` names each region this file writes with its delimiters; `drift()` lifts the region out of the lesson and compares it against what this file would write today.

- **present but different → `DRIFT`, fails**
- **absent → `PENDING`**, reported not failed — ~240 lessons have never been wired, and failing on those would make the instrument permanently red and therefore ignored

## Dual gate, both directions

```
drifted copy — hud loader reverted to an older revision
  DRIFT  .../DRIFTED.html  (hud-loader: 317 bytes on disk vs 304 in wire_lessons.py)
  exit 1

current tree, 503 files
  DRIFT 0 · UNCOVERED 41 · PENDING 289 · ok 214
  exit 0
```

## A correction I made before shipping

My first drift rule was too strict: it also flagged `showSlide` when present in an unrecognised form, producing **41 failures on the current tree**. Investigating rather than accepting them showed those decks are pretty-printed with extra calls the minified one-line patch cannot match:

```js
  function showSlide(i){
    slides.forEach((s,j)=>s.classList.toggle('active', j===i));
    updateProgress();
    checkTimerVisibility();
    updateTABrief();
  }
```

Nothing generated them, so there is no source they diverged from. That is a **coverage gap, not drift**. It now prints `UNCOVERED`, does not fail, and is filed as **IDX-5** with its enumeration command — because the old instrument counted all 41 as passes, so it is a real finding the fix surfaced.

The 289 `PENDING` are the rollout backlog, byte-identical at `cacaf16` before any of the six merges. Not defects.

`build-anim/inject.py` deliberately untouched — permanently red by design, invoked by nothing; retiring it belongs with the `build-anim/` deletion decision.

open_prs.body:
ORDER OM4 Lane C.

The generator's `primary()` picks the first "visible" control to hand focus to after the splash. `visible()` tested `isConnected`, `disabled`, `display`, `visibility` and a non-zero rect — **but not inertness**. An element inside an `inert` subtree passes all of those and still cannot take focus, so `primary()` could hand focus to something unfocusable and leave `activeElement` on `BODY` with no focus event at all.

## Reproduced, not assumed (RL16)

The whole fix rests on `inert` reflecting to a content attribute. Measured in a browser rather than taken from spec:

```
before: { attr: false, closest: false }
app.inert = true
after:  { attr: true,  closest: true  }

oldVisibleSaysVisible: true      ← the current shape calls it visible
activeAfterFocus:      "BODY"    ← and focusing it lands nowhere
```

One guard, inside the existing early return, wrapped so a browser without `closest` or attribute-selector support degrades to the old behaviour rather than throwing inside the splash closure.

## The finding — which is the point of the lane

SS6 re-run across all seven applied routes, at runtime, before and after:

| route | focus lands on | inert ancestor |
|---|---|---|
| echovault | `start-btn` | none |
| medevac | `A` | none |
| neonmeridian | `playBtn` | none |
| rallyvector3d | `startBtn` | none |
| hyperdraft | `mbmhud-back` | none |
| townlife | `startBtn` | none |
| novasiege | `start-run` | none |

**Identical both sides**, 0 inert ancestors on any of them, same focus-event sequences. **None of the seven was relying on the broken behaviour** — this closes a latent hole rather than repairing a live one.

The splash element was present on **7/7** routes, so the probe fired on every route it reported; the harness *throws* rather than reporting a route where no splash appeared (RL17).

## `primary()` needed no change — but the reason is worth recording

`[data-mbm-primary-start]` is already first in its selector list, so the declared-start-selector half of the lane was already satisfied. However, **no applied route uses it**: the attribute appears in each route only *inside* the generated region, as the selector string, and **0 times outside it**. Every route reaches its start control through the positional fallbacks — which is precisely why the inertness hole mattered.

Worth a look separately: `hyperdraft` lands on `mbmhud-back`, the HUD back link, rather than a start control. Legal (it is a real focusable control) but probably not intended.

## Generator-owned throughout

Regenerated through `render_maker_splash.py`, never by hand: **7 applied targets, 7 written, 0 divergent**; `--check` green and a second pass writes 0. The region grows 52 B per route (e.g. novasiege 129,049 → 129,101 B).

open_prs.body:
**Do not merge yet.** This is deliberately held, and the reason is about test order, not code quality.

Depends on #24. Replaces the second half of #23, which is now closed.

## Why it waits

If this ships now and your test submission fails, **the result is uninterpretable** — it could be CORS refused, or the endpoint rejecting an unactivated address. One test, two unknowns, no conclusion, and your thirty seconds buys nothing.

Merge #24 alone and the **plain form** is what you test. That settles activation cleanly and proves the POST path end to end. Only then is this worth a second submission, with one unknown left in it.

## What it does

The bare endpoint returns you to `/thanks/` whether or not anything was delivered. The `/ajax/` endpoint returns JSON, so the page can tell the difference and say so.

**Progressive enhancement, deliberately.** The form's `action` is **unchanged** — still the plain endpoint. The handler intercepts only when `fetch` and `FormData` exist, and any throw before the fetch lets the browser submit normally. *Switching the `action` itself to `/ajax/` was rejected: a visitor with JS off would get a screenful of raw JSON.*

## The unresolved question, stated plainly

**I do not know whether FormSubmit's `/ajax/` endpoint permits a cross-origin request from `madebymatt.uk`.** `formsubmit.co` is unreachable from the build container (403 on CONNECT), so I could not ask it.

All three branches passed **against a stub — 7/7 — and a stub is not the endpoint.**

```
SUCCESS  {"success":"true"}   -> POST to /ajax/…, redirect to /thanks/
FAILURE  {"success":"false"}  -> no redirect, error panel, direct address,
                                 typed text kept, button re-enabled
UNREACHABLE  abort            -> same fallback
```

**The exact test that would settle it:** after #24 is merged and activation is confirmed, merge this, submit once from a browser with the devtools Network tab open, and look at the `POST` to `formsubmit.co/ajax/…`. A CORS failure shows as a blocked request with no readable response; a success shows JSON. If it is blocked, the page correctly says *"the relay could not be reached"* and offers the direct address — safe, but the form would never complete through this path.

**Revert SHA if it misbehaves after merging: `7c20279` — one revert removes it.** Nothing in #24 depends on it.

## The costs, not sold

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| listeners on the form | **0** | **1** (`submit`) |
| listeners on its 7 fields | **0** | **0** |

**Origins — load-time and submit-time are different questions.** No load-time origin is added; `/privacy/`'s enumeration is the *load-time* census and stays at **1** (`api.counterapi.dev`). Submit-time was already `formsubmit.co`; only the path changes.

**Failure is fail-safe by construction.** Every unknown resolves to *"that may not have gone through — here is the direct address"*, the typed text stays in the boxes, the button re-enables, and a 15-second timeout covers a hanging request. The worst case is today's behaviour, not a lost message.

## One more vendor question this raises

Does the `/ajax/` endpoint share the **same activation state** as the plain endpoint, or is it activated separately? If separate, testing this later carries a *second* unknown and the ordering argument above applies all over again. Added to `MATT_UI_CHECKLIST.md` §3 as a question, not an assertion.
